/ai-automation-builder/sales-automation.note: specificity: PRICING CELL OFF-CATEGORY. why_table Emergent pricing: 'Credits, no per-approver seats, no task cap'. Against Salesforce Sales Cloud ('Per user, per month by edition') and HubSpot Sales Hub ('Per seat, per month'), the seat that costs a sales team money is the rep's, not an approver's; 'per-approver seats' is approval-workflow language (catalogue row 8) and 'no task cap' answers Zapier-style task pricing that neither CRM uses. The sales variant in rules/competitors/aab.json has no pricing override, so the hub default leaks in. Library change for Divit: a sales pricing variant built on the approved claim 'the built app has no per-seat pricing', e.g. 'Credits; reps are not billed as seats'. Same class elsewhere: faq10 'runs on credits with no task cap' (answers a per-user question with a task-cap point). GENERIC: meta_title 'Built Around Your Process' could head any hub page; name the sales job instead. | craft: TACKED-ON ', and' ENDINGS: 11 sentences in prose fields bolt a second outcome on after a comma, so the sentence ends on an afterthought, not the important word: feature_2 ', and the outcome is written to the deal record in the CRM.'; feature_3 ', and no rep spends Friday afternoon typing it in.'; tab_content_1 'The rep gets a Slack alert, and the owner is set in HubSpot.'; tab_content_3 ', and its owner gets the deal value in Slack.'; tab_content_4 'The list posts to Slack on Monday, and a renewal opportunity opens in the CRM for each account.'; faq3 'Most CRMs include some of it, and teams that need more add a layer on top.'; faq4 ', and it runs on any CRM, HubSpot and Pipedrive included.'; faq5 ', and managers get a forecast built from the deals that are open today.'; faq8 'A form fill starts a nurture sequence, and a reply books a meeting.'; faq10 ', and it is free to start.'; howto_step_5 ', and it repeats daily until someone acts on it.' Three of four tab paragraphs end this way. Split them or restructure so each sentence carries one idea and ends on it; keep at most two on the page. (tab_content_1 'and the rest rotate across the team' and tab_content_2 'and another email follows on day 3' are real sequences and can stay.) | voice: HEDGE OPENER: faq6 'It depends on where the gap is.' (a machine tell; answer the question first). SAME IDEA TOLD TWICE: features_subheading 'Sales automation is software that runs the repeat work of selling on rules, while reps keep the conversations.' and faq1 'Sales automation is software that handles the admin of selling... Reps keep the work that needs judgment' (same definition, same opener, same 'reps keep' turn); feature_4 'The reminder repeats each morning until someone updates the deal.' and howto_step_5 'it repeats daily until someone acts on it'; howto_description 'Emergent turns those rules into a working app' and howto_step_2 'Emergent turns those sentences into rules'; faq5 'It logs each email and meeting against the deal' restates feature_3 'Sent emails and meeting notes sync to Salesforce or HubSpot'. Each repeated idea should appear once, the second place should add something new (catalogue row 18). | truth: 1) why_table Emergent pricing 'no per-approver seats, no task cap': not meaningful against per-user CRMs (see specificity); Salesforce and HubSpot do not sell by task, so 'no task cap' implies a limit they do not have (catalogue row 8 class). 2) faq4 'No. Salesforce automation means the flows and rules configured inside Salesforce' is stated as settled; 'salesforce automation' is widely used as a spelling of sales force automation (the term predates the company). Answer that it can mean either, then separate them. 3) howto_step_7 'every version of the workflow is saved in your repo' states platform behaviour as automatic (catalogue row 14); the approved claim is code export to GitHub, so write it as something the team does ('push each version to your repo'). 4) tab_content_4 H3 'Start every renewal 90 days before the contract ends' vs the image: the 'Renewal opportunity created' mini is for Hooli at '21 days', which means the opportunity was not started at 90 days; and 'a renewal opportunity opens in the CRM for each account' on a weekly list would reopen duplicates every Monday (also in mockup renewalReminders 'create a renewal opportunity for each account'). Say it opens when an account enters the 90-day window, and draw it for Northwind at 85 days. 5) Cross-tab cast contradicts the copy: Globex is a new inbound demo request routed to M. Rossi (uc-1, cover 'New lead: Globex'), an open $52,000 Evaluation deal (uc-3), and an existing customer at '$64,000 a year' renewing in 63 days under Priya Shah (uc-4). tab_content_1 says each request is 'checked against the CRM for an existing account' and howto_step_2 says 'Named accounts stay with their current owner', so an existing customer cannot land as a new lead with a new owner. Hooli (new 2,400-employee lead in uc-1, '$42,000 a year' customer in uc-4) and Northwind (Proposal deal in uc-3, customer in uc-4) repeat the problem. 6) uc-2: hero line 'Recap opened twice, last on Oct 10' while the timeline says 'Second email, Day 3, opened twice' and shows no opens on the recap. 7) faq8 'a reply books a meeting': a reply does not book anything; say a reply ends the sequence or sends a booking link. | distinct: Nouns swapped from the AP and approval-workflow siblings: howto_step_6 'Run a quarter of real leads and deals through the workflow before go-live... adjust any rule that disagrees by prompting, and replay it until the two lists match.' vs AP howto_step_6 'Run last month's invoices through the automated AP workflow before go-live... fix the rule by prompting and run the sample again until the two match.'; howto_step_7 'every version of the workflow is saved in your repo' vs AP step 7 'Every rule change is versioned in your repo' vs approval-workflow step 7 'with every version kept in exportable code'; why_description 'Sales platforms price by seat and keep your playbook in their app.' vs approval-workflow 'Most approval tools charge per user and keep the audit trail in their app.' and AP 'your approval rules live inside the vendor's app'; feature_6 'Routing rules and sequences export to your GitHub repository... hand the code to one of your engineers' vs AP feature_6 'The matching rules and the approval chain export to your GitHub repository as code your engineers can review.' Write a sales-specific dry run (e.g. a shadow week where the app suggests owners and reps accept or reassign) and a sales-specific go-live and why line. | faq: Exactly 10 on-topic items, hub link in item 2, sibling links to crm-automation, lead-nurturing-workflow and approval-workflow read naturally. Labs; 'Vandelay' (uc-1 table) is the Seinfeld gag. Replace all four with neutral invented names.
